messages:
amanda: Heads up — pharma POC kickoff with Acme Biomed. Need to scope success criteria + model fit. They require private deployment option, tool-calling to an internal drug DB, and long-document support (they mentioned ~"100k words"). Can we align tomorrow?

luke: Got it. Sales timeline from customer: 2-week pilot then 3mo eval. Who's taking technical lead?

raj: I can own model-fit + evals. Quick clarifying Qs: expected throughput? synchronous latency SLOs? And do they need real-time tool calling or async webhooks?

amanda: Throughput is small — ~30 reqs/min. They want sync responses for triage UI (p95 target ~<400ms for short queries). For long-doc summarization async is fine. Tool calling needs to hit their internal QA DB with authenticated requests (customer-managed creds).

ben: For "100k words" we shouldn't try a single 100k context LLM. Recommend retrieval + rerank pipeline: chunk docs, dense retrieval (embeddings), then reranker (cross-encoder) + generator. If they insist on extremely long context we can offer a hybrid with segment-level generation and stitching. Models: rwd-32k-v2 (for most), rwd-65k for extended docs; avoid unvalidated 100k single-pass.

sophie: Proposed POC success metrics (draft):
- Retrieval MRR uplift >= 0.12 vs current baseline
- Precision@5 for regulatory facts >= 0.85
- Hallucination incidents < 5% on a labeled set
- End-to-end p95 (retrieve+rerank+gen) < 1s for typical queries
- Cost per 1k queries within budget (TBD)

emma: Security checklist: they require SOC2 + EU/US data residency options, KMS/HSM for key management, audit logs, and a no-persistent-retention configuration for POC data. I'll start the security questionnaire. Also need clarification on whether customer will allow outbound calls from Private to their DB or they want a VPN.

sec-bot: Security questionnaire draft uploaded: https://redwood/internal/sec/acme-pharma-poc/sq-draft-v1 (shared with @emma and @luke)

raj: Eval plan sketch: collect 200 customer-supplied prompts (70% retrieval/search, 30% summarization). Steps:
1) Build embedding index (1536d) in FAISS
2) Compare retrieval models (our default embedding vs s-BERT)
3) Run cross-encoder reranker on top-10 candidates to compute MRR/Recall@10
4) Generate answers with rwd-32k-v2 for short tasks, rwd-65k for longer contexts
Target perf: reranker latency < 200ms for top-10 on dedicated tiny pool.

amanda: Pricing question from customer: estimate for 3-week POC with hosted infra vs tiny dedicated pool. Ballpark: hosted with standard models ~ $6k for expected usage, dedicated reserved tiny pool ~ $18k (includes setup + reserved). Luke — can sales offer a credit?

luke: I'll propose a $5k credit + usage overage terms. Need finance approval; I'll ping finance today.

emma: Note on Private/on-prem: our Private deployment lead time ~4 weeks (standard). If customer insists <4w we can scope a constrained sandbox in their VPC but limited scale and no full auditability. Flagging for contract.

ben: Quick implementation stub for the eval runner we plan to hand to the customer:
```
# eval runner (python psuedo)
for q in sample_queries:
    ctx = retrieve(q, top_k=100)
    reranked = cross_encoder.rank(ctx)[:10]
    prompt = f"Sources:\n{reranked[:3]}\nUser: {q}\n"
    gen = generate(prompt, model='rwd-32k-v2', max_tokens=512)
    log(q, len(ctx), tokens(gen), latency(gen))
```
Log both tokens and latencies for billing + SLOs.

raj: For embeddings use 1536d vectors and FAISS HNSW. We'll measure recall@10, MRR and embed cost. If reranker is expensive we can do two-stage (approximate cheap reranker then cross-encoder on top-3).

sophie: Tentative POC timeline:
- Day 0-3: security Q + contract + data access prep
- Day 1-5: customer provides sample data + prompt sets
- Day 5-9: model fit and embedding baseline comparisons
- Day 10-14: integrate tool-calling auth + dev sandbox
- Day 15-21: run evals, tuning, handover to customer for QA
Is this acceptable?

amanda: Looks good. Action items: Emma starts SQ + uploads; Raj runs initial fit tomorrow; Ben preps eval runner; Luke prepares credit ask for finance; Sophie drafts final success criteria doc. I'll sync with customer tomorrow 11:00am PST.

luke: :thumbsup:

ben: I'll also capture a short perf matrix (p95 gen, rerank latency, token cost) so we can iterate pricing if needed.

amanda: Thanks — keeping thread open. I'll post updates after the customer sync.
thread_text: pharma POC kickoff: scoping, model fit, tooling, pricing, security
